parsed.why: Constitutional equality, hate-crime statute, LGR and a binding 2025 ruling compelling trans-inmate care show working recourse; but township violence against trans people, police mockery of mismatched IDs, and unremedied facility-access inequality remain documented exposures.

No LGR, no anti-discrimination or hate-crime route, hostile attitudes (73% capital hostility), and documented state and non-state harassment, extortion and violence — with police invoking the ambiguous sexuality provision as an extraction lever against gender-nonconforming people.

Constitutional gender-identity protection, protected bathroom access, surgery-free LGR including nonbinary, hate-crime coverage and regional-low victimisation; negatives are prison-practice lag (remedied by damages), low reporting, and a pending asylum-detention case, not visitor-facing bans.

Never criminalised same-sex conduct and documents no trans-specific targeting; but no anti-discrimination law, official blocking of LGBT content, media silence, single advocacy group, and tradition-linked gender-diverse visibility with otherwise thin record warrant cautious middle-upper placement.

Passed bill criminalising trans identification and cross-dressing awaiting expected assent, existing 'unnatural carnal knowledge' offence, documented mob justice, state closures of LGBTQ centres, no LGR or protection: imprisonment risk with no working recourse.
